title: Overbudget Haar-Purity Subsystem Designs Beyond the Quadratic Threshold

canonical_object.scheme: Folded Johnson association scheme J_bar(2k, k)
canonical_object.overlap_discrepancy: g_ab = 4 * |A_a intersect A_b| - n in [-n, n]
canonical_object.objective: S_{n,d}(F) = sum_{a<b} h_{n,d}(g_ab), quadratic proxy Q(F) = sum_{a<b} g_ab^2

theorems.label: Theorem 1
theorems.summary: Exact alphabet dichotomy: E(s^2) and Haar optimization coincide identically for n in {6,8,10} (<=2 off-diagonal |g| values) and diverge strictly for every even n >= 12, witnessed uniformly across all integers d >= 2 at n=12 (m in {20,40,50,60,140,220}) and n=14 (m in {40,80,140}).

theorems.label: Theorem 2
theorems.summary: Closed-form folded Johnson eigenvalue formula Lambda_i(n,d) = sum_{r=i}^k (d^2 - 1)^r * binom(k-i, k-r) * binom(2k-r-i, k-r) with strict monotonicity Lambda_0 > Lambda_2 > ... > Lambda_{2*floor(k/2)} > 0 and exact recovery of the E(s^2) quadratic floor Q(F) >= n^2/(2(n-1)) * m * (m - n + 1) from Q_2(delta).

theorems.label: Theorem 3
theorems.summary: At n=12, Delsarte LP gives c_8(F) >= max(0, m(m-66)/22) with equality iff Pi_2 1_F = Pi_4 1_F = 0; S(5,6,12)/Z_2 uniquely achieves m=66, and explicit 2-class and 3-class dual polynomials prove dimension-uniform global optimality across all integers d >= 2 at m in {11,22,55,66,132,330,396,462}.

theorems.label: Theorem 4
theorems.summary: Parseval row-sum identity R_{n,d} = (1/(2*pi)) * integral_{-pi}^{pi} ((d+1)^2 - 4d*sin^2(theta/2))^k dtheta ~ ((d+1)/sqrt(d)) * ((d+1)/2)^n * M_n and overbudget sandwich max(0, (m/2)*((m/M_n)*R_{n,d} - (d^n+1))) <= B_{n,d}(m) <= (m(m-1)/(2(M_n-1)))*(R_{n,d} - d^n - 1), yielding B_{n,d}(m) = ((d+1)/(2*sqrt(d))) * m^2 * ((d+1)/2)^n * (1 + o(1)) whenever m/M_n >> sqrt(n) * (d/(d+1))^n.

prior_work_relation.author: Ryosuke Shiroshita
prior_work_relation.scope: Resolves the square Hadamard budget m = n for n in {6,8,10,12,14,16} using the 0-4 minorant.
prior_work_relation.extension_here: Resolves the overbudget regime m > n across 1 <= m <= M_n, establishing E(s^2)-vs-Haar separation for n >= 12, folded Johnson spectral monotonicity, Witt S(5,6,12)/Z_2 LP phase transition, and asymptotic Parseval collapse.

verification.dependencies: Python 3 standard library only (zero floating-point relaxations for core identities and certificates)
